misreading: No semantic defect is common to all four (F1 looks spec-correct); the shared traits are that pub struct Cron derives nothing, so hidden tests using Cron::parse(..).unwrap_err() or assert_eq! on the Result fail to compile, and is_ascii_whitespace() misses VT (0x0B) for R2 Layout. (Also, not shared: F2 rejects step 60/24 [R8], F3 reports oversized steps as Bounds [R5/R8], F4 gives Syntax(start+1) for *-prefixed bases like **, *-5, *x/2 [R7/R9].)
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible tests only unwrap() a successful Cron::parse (needs CronError: Debug only), never inspect a parse error, and never use non-space control whitespace.
prevention: Derive the stated common traits on every public type that can appear inside a returned Result, unless explicitly forbidden; tests may unwrap_err or compare.

misreading: Caret/tilde operands that parse as full three-field versions get only the inclusive lower bound (the guard `if p.k < 3 || p.full.is_none()` skips the exclusive upper), so ^1.2.3 matches 9.0.0 and ~1.2.3 matches 1.9.0. (Also: R25/R32 caret/tilde Syntax offsets at token start not operand start; R23 unspaced leading/trailing || gives Syntax and empty arms beat earlier malformed arms; R57 index-order not lexicographic min conflict; R42/R45 only pre=0 probed at anchors.)
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: Visible tests only check that versions inside ^2.1.0 and ~2.5.0 match, never that a version above the implied upper bound is rejected; no unspaced, empty or malformed || arms and no multi-label conflicts.
prevention: For every generated or implied bound, test values just beyond each boundary, not only values comfortably inside the accepted set.

misreading: Under ErrorPolicy::Stop, the failing row is pushed and returned at the first error. It therefore holds only the successful prefix plus one None, instead of None for the failing spec and every later spec (row length < columns.len()).
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: The only visible Stop test has no failing cell, so it only exercises the success path.
prevention: On early-exit paths, still emit outputs in the full required shape, filling placeholders for every unprocessed position.

misreading: All files read the lowercase word in the template "T skip ID dependency" as a placeholder and print the blocking dependency ID instead of the literal word dependency. (Not shared: F1/F2 also sort skip lines per propagation round rather than across the whole transitive closure.)
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: No visible test has a terminally failed job with dependents, so no skip line is ever emitted.
prevention: In output templates, treat only uppercase or explicitly defined tokens as placeholders; emit lowercase words verbatim as literals.

misreading: Context components (cwd or home) are pushed with no link lookup because the expand_top helper is a no-op stub, so a link whose path equals a cwd/home prefix is never expanded. Tilde expansion also uses raw rather than normalized home components, leaking . and .. into results.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: In the visible relative-link test the link sits below cwd and is hit by a request component; no test puts a link on the cwd or home path or uses dot segments in home.
prevention: Never ship stubbed no-op helpers; apply the same per-step processing (lookups, validation) to every input source the spec says is traversed.

misreading: decode_many preallocates Vec::with_capacity(count) from the caller-supplied count. A huge count (e.g. usize::MAX) panics with capacity overflow, or aborts on allocation, before any byte is read, instead of returning Truncated.
visible_tests_would_not_catch_because: The visible batch test uses count=2; no extreme count is exercised.
prevention: Never preallocate or size buffers from untrusted caller-supplied counts; grow incrementally so huge counts fail gracefully with the specified error.
